description: Replace Family Pulse's local-only institution removal with a true Plaid disconnect flow that calls /item/remove, stops future sync and billing, and preserves local historical data by default. Add a separate destructive purge path for users who intentionally want to erase local institution history.

timing.gatingCondition: None. This should be executed first because the current local-only delete risks continued Plaid billing after users believe an institution has been removed.

principles: Disconnect should stop remote sync and billing while preserving local historical reporting by default
Permanent local data deletion must be a separate destructive action, not the default interpretation of disconnect
Remote disconnect should call Plaid /item/remove before changing local institution state
Users must understand the difference between disconnect, reauth, and purge
Disconnected institutions should no longer be eligible for routine syncs
Server-side secrets invariant remains unchanged — no Plaid access tokens or internal removal details leak to clients

techStack.database: PostgreSQL item lifecycle state on items and/or related tables
techStack.testing: node:test integration tests for remote disconnect, local archival, and explicit purge behavior

userStories.title: Disconnect an institution remotely while preserving history
acceptanceCriteria: A parent can disconnect a linked institution from Plaid using a dedicated disconnect action
The backend calls Plaid /item/remove before marking the institution disconnected locally
On success, the institution stops future syncs and billing-oriented Plaid usage
Local accounts and transactions remain available for historical reporting by default
The institution is shown in the UI as disconnected or archived rather than silently disappearing
userStories.testStrategy: Integration test stubbing Plaid item removal and verifying local state transitions without cascading historical deletion.

userStories.title: Separate purge from disconnect
acceptanceCriteria: A distinct destructive action exists for permanently deleting local institution history
Purge requires explicit confirmation that local accounts and transactions will be deleted
Purge does not masquerade as the normal disconnect path
If retained, any old delete semantics are renamed so users cannot confuse them with disconnect
userStories.testStrategy: Route-level integration test verifying purge deletes local rows only when explicitly invoked.

userStories.title: Exclude disconnected institutions from future sync runs
acceptanceCriteria: Disconnected institutions remain queryable for historical display
Operational logs and status views distinguish disconnected items from broken items that need reauth
No existing good item is skipped unless explicitly disconnected
Feature 14 defines reconnect semantics explicitly enough that archived local history is not silently duplicated by future implementation work
userStories.testStrategy: Sync integration test verifying disconnected items are not included in the sync loop.

userStories.title: Clarify institution lifecycle actions in Settings
acceptanceCriteria: Settings uses explicit labels for Disconnect, Fix login, and any destructive purge action
Disconnect confirmation explains that Plaid billing/sync stops while history stays by default
Purge confirmation explains that local history will be erased
Users can still see enough institution state to understand whether the item is active, disconnected, or broken
userStories.testStrategy: Manual UI verification in Settings plus route smoke tests.

high: Changing delete semantics touches item/account/transaction lifecycle and can destroy history if implemented incorrectly
medium: Plaid /item/remove may fail for already-broken Items, so fallback handling and messaging must be explicit
Archived-history behavior will affect future reconnect semantics and must not accidentally re-enable sync
low: Some users may still expect disconnect to remove all traces locally, which is why purge remains available separately

preFlightChecklist: Decide the exact local representation of a disconnected institution (items.status extension or dedicated fields)
Confirm how disconnected institutions should appear in Settings and status views
Confirm whether purge remains supported after remote disconnect and what sequence is allowed
Confirm the app should not call Plaid for disconnected items during status or sync operations
Choose and document reconnect semantics for archived-history items before coding begins
